title: Symphony No. 5 in C minor
hook: Four notes, and everything that can be built from them.

painting.title: Snow Storm: Hannibal and his Army Crossing the Alps
painting.pairingNote: A struggle through darkness with light breaking at the edge of the storm, painted within four years of the symphony.

facts: First performed on 22 December 1808 in Vienna, in a four-hour concert that also introduced the Sixth Symphony and the Fourth Piano Concerto.
A single rhythm (short, short, short, long) appears in all four movements.
The symphony travels from C minor to C major: from struggle to blazing light.
Beethoven holds back trombones, piccolo and contrabassoon until the finale. Their entry is one of the great arrivals in music.
bigPicture.inOneLine: struggle (I), consolation with flashes of hope (II), a ghostly march (III), victory (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro con brio
movements.summary: The most famous opening in classical music, and a lesson in economy: nearly every bar of this [[sonata-form|sonata form]] movement is made from the first four notes.

mainIdeas.name: The motto
mainIdeas.description: short, short, short, long. It is both the theme and the accompaniment.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a soft, rising melody in the violins, announced by a horn call.

stops.hear: The four-note motto, twice, each time ending on a held note
stops.happening: The motto. For a moment we cannot even tell the key

stops.hear: The motto stacked up through the strings, quietly, then louder
stops.happening: Theme 1 is assembled entirely from the motto

stops.hear: A loud horn call, then a gentle melody in violins and woodwinds
stops.happening: Theme 2. Listen below it: cellos and basses keep tapping the motto

stops.hear: The opening returns
stops.happening: The [[exposition|exposition]] is repeated

stops.hear: The motto in distant keys; then single chords passed between woodwinds and strings, quieter and quieter
stops.happening: The [[development|development]]. The horn call is reduced to two notes, then one

stops.hear: The motto crashes back in the full orchestra
stops.happening: The [[recapitulation|recapitulation]]

stops.hear: Everything stops for a lone, plaintive oboe
stops.happening: A tiny [[cadenza|cadenza]]. Time stands still for a few seconds

stops.hear: A new, stamping march; the music will not stop
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]], almost as long as a second development. It ends firmly in the minor

notice: Follow the motto into the background. Even under the gentle second theme it never leaves.
The oboe solo is the only moment of stillness in the movement.

movements.heading: Andante con moto
movements.summary: Two themes take turns and are decorated a little more each time: a set of [[variation|variation]]s. One theme is gentle; the other keeps breaking into a fanfare that foreshadows the finale.

stops.hear: Violas and cellos sing a relaxed, graceful melody
stops.happening: Theme A

stops.hear: Clarinets and bassoons begin softly; then trumpets and drums burst out in a bright fanfare
stops.happening: Theme B, turning suddenly to C major. A glimpse of the victory to come

stops.hear: Theme A again, now in smoothly flowing notes
stops.happening: First variation

stops.hear: The same, in faster notes; then taken over by the basses
stops.happening: Second variation

stops.hear: Woodwinds alone, hesitant
stops.happening: An interlude

stops.hear: Theme A in the full orchestra
stops.happening: The grandest statement

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: A bassoon picks up the tune at a quicker pace
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]

notice: The fanfare of Theme B uses the same short-short-short-long rhythm as the motto, in disguise.

movements.heading: Scherzo: Allegro
movements.summary: A [[scherzo|scherzo]] that begins in whispers, is interrupted by the motto, and ends in one of the most famous transitions ever written.

stops.hear: Cellos and basses creep upward in near silence
stops.happening: A ghostly opening

stops.hear: Horns blast out a hammering rhythm
stops.happening: The motto again: short, short, short, long

stops.hear: Cellos and basses scurry gruffly; the other strings join in turn
stops.happening: The [[trio|trio]], in C major, starting like a [[fugue|fugue]]

stops.hear: The opening returns as a shadow: plucked strings and a quiet bassoon
stops.happening: The scherzo comes back in [[pizzicato|pizzicato]], as if afraid to wake someone

stops.hear: A soft drum taps over a long held note; violins feel their way upward
stops.happening: The transition. Tension builds for almost a minute, then runs straight into the finale without a break

movements.heading: Allegro
movements.summary: C major, full orchestra, and three instruments that have been silent until now. The finale is the answer to the first movement.

stops.hear: A blaze of brass on three rising notes
stops.happening: Theme 1. Trombones, piccolo and contrabassoon play for the first time

stops.hear: A striding tune in the horns
stops.happening: A second idea in the same triumphant mood

stops.hear: A quick, skipping figure in the violins
stops.happening: Theme 2

stops.label: Middle
stops.hear: The skipping figure is worked up to a great climax
stops.happening: The [[development|development]]

stops.label: After the climax
stops.hear: Sudden quiet: the tapping rhythm of the scherzo returns
stops.happening: A memory of the third movement. The darkness is recalled, then swept away again

stops.label: Shortly after
stops.hear: The blaze returns
stops.happening: The [[recapitulation|recapitulation]]

stops.label: Last 2 minutes
stops.hear: The music speeds up; chord after chord of C major
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]. Beethoven hammers the home chord as if to make sure

notice: The return of the scherzo inside the finale was unprecedented. Triumph means more because the shadow comes back first.

threads.title: Minor to major
threads.body: The whole symphony is a single journey from C minor to C major.

threads.title: Held-back forces
threads.body: The finale sounds bigger because Beethoven saved instruments for it.
